summary: Tested two new features: (1) Overview calendar date-picker (calendar icon, month-view modal, color-coded days, day tap navigation, month nav, close/backdrop dismiss, legend) and (2) Dragons page 'Vægt og plejeplan' pill button replacing the old top-right weight icon. Both features work correctly end-to-end (backend + UI). Verified GET /api/completions/calendar-summary logic is correct via direct manipulation (toggled tasks on 2026-07-05 to force 'green', confirmed in UI, then reverted). Found one notable behavior-design nuance (not a hard bug) around automatic tasks always counting as 'completed' in the calendar summary, meaning RED ('nothing logged') can never actually occur given the current careplan (every day/age-category combo has 2 automatic light tasks). Regression checks (dragon list, edit/delete buttons, dragons untouched) all pass.

minor.issue: Automatic (is_automatic=true) schedule slots are always counted as 'completed' in this endpoint regardless of date/actual completion record, and every day_of_week x age_category combination in the current careplan has exactly 2 automatic slots (light/heat tasks) per dragon. Net effect: the 'red' (Intet registreret / nothing logged) status can never occur in practice since automatic tasks always contribute non-zero completed count - only 'yellow' or 'green' will ever show. This matches daily-overview's own automatic-task display style (no manual toggle for automatic tasks) so it may be intentional, but worth confirming with product intent since the legend advertises 3 distinct states and one is effectively unreachable under normal usage.

action_items: Confirm with product whether 'red' status being practically unreachable (due to automatic tasks always counting as completed) is intended behavior, or if automatic tasks should be excluded from the completed/total calculation used for calendar day coloring.
No code fixes required otherwise - both features work as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: OverviewCalendarModal.tsx is clean, well-structured, uses proper testIDs, handles loading state, cancels stale API requests via a 'cancelled' flag pattern - good practice.

overview.py calendar-summary endpoint correctly handles brumation activity_state (excludes 'fodring' category) and caches schedule_slots lookups per (day_of_week, age_category, activity_state) key to avoid redundant queries within the month loop - decent perf awareness.

dragons.tsx: weight button correctly relocated below age badge with same testID pattern `dragon-weight-button-{id}` preserved; delete-only icon remains in top-right cardActions row as specified. No stray reference to old weight icon location found in the file.
No MongoDB _id leakage found in /api/completions/calendar-summary or /api/dragons responses.
seed_data_creation: None. Temporarily toggled 6 completions on 2026-07-05 for both dragons (Sif, logan) to verify 'green' status rendering in the calendar, then reverted all 6 back to incomplete afterward - verified completions collection is back to 0 documents / status back to 'yellow' matching original state. Dragons Sif and logan were not modified/deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both new features (overview calendar modal + dragons weight/careplan pill button) are fully working. DB completions collection was empty (0 documents) at start of this test session - likely reset by a prior iteration's 'Reset & load care plan' test (iteration_20). All calendar-summary days across Jan-Jul 2026 showed 'yellow' before my test since only automatic tasks contribute completions and no manual completions existed anywhere. I verified 'green' rendering by temporarily completing manual tasks on 2026-07-05 then reverted - final state confirmed back to yellow (completed=4/total=10) matching pre-test baseline. Dragons Sif/logan untouched (verified via GET /api/dragons before and after).
rca_of_issue: Not applicable - no bugs found, only a design observation documented in backend_issues.minor regarding the 'red' status being practically unreachable given automatic tasks always count toward completion in the calendar-summary aggregation.
